content:
jess: Hey team — customer reports 401 invalid_api_key when calling our hosted /v1/generate from a web form. Same key works from curl. Any ideas?

rahul: Can you paste the exact request headers + body (sanitized) so we can see how the browser is sending it?

jess: Pasted (sanitized):
```
Authorization: Apikey  abcdEFGHIJKL==
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
```
body (raw form payload): `api_key=%3CabcdEFGHIJKL%3E&prompt=hello` — looks HTML-escaped/encoded.

amy: Two red flags: 1) header says `Apikey` (capitalization + extra space before token) — our header parser is strict and leading spaces will cause token validation to fail. 2) body shows `<`/`>` encoded which suggests the client is double-encoding or the form input included angle brackets. Either could produce a malformed token string.

jess: The customer says they copy/pasted the key into an old HTML form and submit via JS. Curl test uses `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` and succeeds. They also have a Chrome extension that injects headers.

rahul: Repro I did locally: simple form with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and JS `fetch('/proxy', {method:'POST', headers:{ 'Authorization': 'Apikey ' + key }})`. Browser/posting will encode `+` and spaces; some extensions rewrite or normalize the header name (e.g., `Authorization` -> `Proxy-Authorization`) which causes our server to drop it. Also seen `Apikey` vs `Bearer` confusion cause intermittent 401s.

ryan: Quick checks to ask customer: 1) Try sending the same request with `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` (no extra spaces) 2) Try `x-api-key: <KEY>` header instead of putting key into form body 3) Disable any header-modifying extensions or test in incognito. If they used an HTML input that included `<`/`>` those chars may have been submitted; tell them to trim/clean the value before sending.

jess: I gave steps + minimal repro snippet and recommended rotating the key and creating a new one to be safe. I also asked them to test with `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>"` and provide the full raw request captured via devtools.

support-bot: automated-scan: observed token value with non-base64 chars and leading whitespace -> validation failure reason: malformed_api_key (mapped to 401 invalid_api_key).

ryan: Docs link I sent: https://redwood.inference/docs/auth#api-keys (includes header examples and common causes). Also suggested enabling short TTL for rotated key and monitoring failed auth in Console.

jess: Customer followed steps, disabled extension, re-sent using `Authorization: Bearer` and it succeeded. They rotated the key and confirmed resolution. Closing on our side. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: tags: escalated:auth, resolution: rotated-key
